title: Tummy-Time Provocations
strapline: Something lovely just within reach, and a warm face at floor level — good reasons for a little one to lift their head and push up.
intent: Give the youngest babies motivating reasons to spend time on their tummies, building the neck, shoulder and back strength that underpins rolling, sitting and crawling.
Turn tummy time from a task to be endured into an invitation — a treasure to reach, a mirror to meet, a face to find.
Offer rich, close-up sensory interest for a baby whose whole world, at this moment, is the small patch of floor in front of them.
Build connection and communication as a key person lies down at the baby's level, face to face.
Keep every session responsive — led by the baby's cues, ending the moment it stops being enjoyable.
implementation: Lay a clean, comfortable surface — a firm mat, a textured blanket, a sheepskin — and place the baby on their tummy for short, frequent stretches.
Position something worth lifting the head for just in reach: a low safety mirror, a treasure, a sensory bottle, an open book, your own face.
Lie down at their level, meet their eyes, talk and sing softly — you are the best provocation in the room.
Start with a minute or two and build gradually; a rolled towel under the chest helps a baby who tires quickly.
Watch for the cues — fussing, face-planting, going quiet — and turn the baby over the moment tummy time stops being a pleasure.
key_questions: Can you see your face in the mirror down here?
Look how you lifted your head to find me!
What's this crinkly blanket like under your hands?
Shall we reach for the shiny bottle together?
Are you telling me you've had enough now?

impact.text: Babies push up on their arms and lift their heads during tummy time, gaining the strength for rolling, sitting and crawling in turn.
A baby reaches for a treasure just within range, exploring the floor world with hands and mouth.
Face down at the mirror and blanket, babies take in texture, reflection and shine with every sense.
With their key person lying face to face, a baby turns to the voice, holds the gaze and babbles back.

enhancements: A low, unbreakable mirror propped at floor level for face-to-face discovery.
A tummy-time treasure line — a sensory bottle, a crinkly book, a soft ball — set just within reach.
Textured blankets and mats — corduroy, satin edging, a sheepskin — for the hands and cheeks pressed against them.
Black-and-white and high-contrast cards for the youngest eyes to study.
A rolled towel or nursing cushion under the chest to support a baby who tires quickly.

playing_exploring: The baby explores the close-up floor world through touch, sight and mouth.
A tempting treasure or a warm face invites the baby to reach and push up freely.
active_learning: Babies work hard to lift and hold their heads, trying again and clearly proud of each new push-up.
creating_thinking: A baby connects their own effort to the reward — head up, and the mirror-face appears.
